attempts.reasoning: Pushed the most advanced passed pawn to h7. This creates an immediate threat of promotion on h8. Even if Black plays Rxc5+, the pawn is only one square from promotion, and the Queen will be decisive. Rejected quiet king moves as the pawn race is the priority. · goal: Promote h-pawn to Queen · plan: Promote the h-pawn: push h6-h7-h8 and use the resulting Queen to force a mate. If Black captures c5, the promotion is still faster than any Rook counterplay.

The knight on g4 is a significant nuisance, threatening h2 and e3. By playing h3, I force the knight to move or be captured. Moving the knight from f3 (Ng5, Nd4) was refuted by the immediate mate threat Qxh2#. h3 addresses the king safety issue and gains a tempo on the knight. While it allows Rxf3 or exf3, I have sufficient defenders (Rook f1, Bishop e2, Pawn g2) to make the exchange acceptable, or simply force the knight to retreat first. · goal: Force the knight on g4 to move or capture it. · plan: Repel the knight on g4 and stabilize king safety. Once the knight is driven back or traded, I will look to utilize my bishop pair and control the open f-file.
